cleaningPolicy: Formatting cleanup only. No substantive rewriting. Paragraph breaks preserved where present.

speakers.bio: Dr. Sayed Moustafa al-Qazwini is the Founding Imam of the Islamic Educational Center of Orange County and Founding President of the Shia Muslim Council of Southern California. He is a graduate of the Islamic seminary of Qum, holds a PhD in Islamic Studies from UK and is the author of a number of books. Shortly after his arrival in California in 1994, Dr. Sayed Moustafa al-Qazwini became the founder and imam of the Islamic Cultural Center of San Diego, California. This center was the first Shia mosque established in San Diego County for religious and social events. His success in San Diego paved the way for his next mission—a mosque in Orange County, California. In September 1996, he founded the Islamic Educational Center of Orange County (IECOC). Drawing on his experience in Islamic studies, he has maturated the center for educational, religious and social events. As the founder and imam of IECOC, he serves as a mentor for the Muslim community. Dr. al-Qazwini’s associations are also founding member of the council of Shia Muslim Scholars of North America, Co-chair of the West Coast Dialogue of Muslims and Catholics, a senior advisor for the United Muslim American Association and the founder of Ahlulbayt Islamic Seminary of California. Dr. al-Qazwini spends much of his time lecturing across the United States and the world, and participating in interfaith and intrafaith dialogues and various panels at churches and universities.

Dr. Sayed Ammar Nakshawani is an Islamic Lecturer, Scholar, Historian & Author. He is known for his knowledge of Islamic History and Qur’anic Exegesis, as well as his ability to convey complex ideas in a clear and engaging manner. His lectures are viewed worldwide and have been translated into multiple languages, making him a popular and influential figure among the global Muslim community.

Sayed Ammar has previously held the role as Associate and Research Director at the Project on Shi’ism and Global Affairs at Harvard University and was the Inaugural Imam Ali Chair of Shi’a Studies at the Hartford Seminary. He also served as Visiting Scholar at Columbia University’s Middle East Institute and the Department of Islamic Studies at the University of Cambridge. He obtained his doctorate from the University of Exeter where he published his dissertation on authority and leadership in early Islam.

Dr. Nakshawani was appointed as a Special Representative to the United Nations promoting women’s rights initiatives, social development, and religious tolerance and is currently listed as one the World’s 500 most influential Muslims.

Sheikh Fadhel Al-Sahlani is a prominent Shia Islamic scholar and religious leader based in New York. Originally from Iraq, Sheikh Al-Sahlani has served for many years at the Imam Al-Khoei Islamic Center in Queens, New York, where he has been involved in religious education, community leadership, and the development of Shia institutions in North America.

He currently serves as the North American Representative of Grand Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Al-Hussaini Al-Sistani, providing religious guidance and answering questions on matters of Islamic jurisprudence. Through his work with the Imam Al-Khoei Foundation, he has played an important role in serving the Shia Muslim community across North America.

Known for his scholarship and community engagement, Sheikh Al-Sahlani regularly addresses topics related to Islamic jurisprudence, spirituality, the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (AS), and the needs of Muslim communities in North America. He has also participated in interfaith and broader community initiatives focused on dialogue, understanding, and peaceful coexistence.

Nazar Al Qatari is an internationally acclaimed artist and Qari, renowned for his captivating recitations of Qasidas, Latmiyas, and Nohas in multiple languages, including Arabic, Urdu, Farsi, and English. Through his soulful voice and heartfelt melodies, he connects audiences around the world to the love of the Holy Ahlulbayt (a.s) and devotion to the Almighty (SWT).

In addition to his artistic achievements, Nazar Al Qatari is deeply committed to humanitarian work. In 2023, he was appointed Goodwill Ambassador for the Imam Hussein Charity, recognizing his ongoing efforts to support vulnerable children and families worldwide. He has actively participated in humanitarian missions, including visits to Iraq to raise awareness for the charity’s relief efforts, and has been praised for his advocacy for the rights of women and children in developing nations.

Beyond his charitable endeavors, Nazar also serves as a judge on The Shia Voice, where he helps discover and mentor emerging talent in the global Shia community.

Nazar Al Qatari wants to make a real difference in the lives of the poor and needy and has set up two academies alongside Imam Hussein Charity, which are skills training projects that could directly lift not just the individual but a family out of poverty. We have carefully selected 50 men to join the Al Abbas Duas Come True Academy that will give them skills training in being a barber or driver and IHC will support them through their apprenticeship for a year. Alongside this, 50 women including widows will join the Sayeeda Zainab Empowerment Academy where they will learn to sew and later if they wish can comfortably earn from tailoring. This project is unique in uplifting a household out of vulnerability by giving them an a skill set that could directly lead to an income and make them stable and secure.

Mehdi Hasan is a journalist and broadcaster, known for his work on the Al Jazeera network and MSNBC, and for his critical commentary on political and social issues. He has hosted programs like The Mehdi Hasan Show on MSNBC and is the founder of the digital media company Zeteo. Hasan is also the author of several books, a skilled debater, and has used his platform to advocate for issues such as Muslim rights, critiques of media bias, and Palestinian freedom

Zahra Al Alawi is a prominent public speaker and television presenter specialising in religious and social issues. She holds a degree in Media and Television from the University of Hertfordshire, UK, and has received personal mentorship from esteemed Islamic scholars and lecturers.

With over 20 years of international experience in public speaking and broadcasting, Zahra has become a well recognised voice within the Muslim community. She is best known for hosting the long running talk show "Woman's View" on Ahlulbayt TV, which features over 300 episodes and a wide range of interviews with women from diverse backgrounds.

Zahra has made numerous appearances on major British media outlets including BBC, ITV3, and Channel 4, where she has addressed various Islamic and societal topics. Her insights have also been featured in national newspapers such as The Telegraph and The Independent.

In 2016, Zahra met with the British Prime Minister at 10 Downing Street, where she highlighted the contributions and achievements of British Muslim women.

She currently hosts “The Zahra Alawi Podcast”, offering in-depth discussions on faith, identity, and contemporary issues.
Sayed Mazen al-Mourtada is the current custodian of the Shrine of Sayeda Zainab in Damascus, Syria. He inherited the custodianship of the prominent Shi'i holy site from his late father, Hani Mohsen.

Shaykh Ramadhan is the Chairman of Ramadhan Foundation, a senior member of Majlis al-Shura (consultative council) of Markazi Jamat E Ahle Sunnat UK and Overseas (Central Association of Sunni Muslims UK & Overseas) which is the oldest (established 1979) and largest body representing Sunni Muslims in the UK; member of Dār al Iftaʾwal Iʿtiqād (The Centre for Doctrines and Beliefs) Birmingham UK; board Member at The Centre for Intra-Muslim Studies (CIMS); and advisor for Markfield Institute of Higher Education BA Islamic programmes. He is the son of the great Gnostic Shaykh Muhammad Ramadhan.

Shaykh Ramadhan became the youngest person to be interviewed on the world’s renowned BBC HardTalk to discuss the July 7th terrorist attacks in London and the response from the Muslim community in the UK. With a high media profile focused on imparting Islamic knowledge to both Muslims and non-Muslims alike, he has delivered lectures throughout the world on a variety of topics including the Muslim role in the West, interfaith and peaceful co-existence. One of his central messages is to promote tolerance and peaceful co-existence. His search for the truth has taken him to various places of the world from the deserts of Mauritania to Morocco, Egypt and Europe. Shaykh Ramadhan currently resides with his family in Greater Manchester.

Anisa Diab is a Muslim counselor and faith-based mental health professional, dedicated to helping Muslims navigate life's challenges with confidence and faith. Anisa's work focuses on providing a safe space for Muslims to discuss their mental health and well-being, blending contemporary counseling techniques with Islamic principles

Sajjad Rizvi is an intellectual historian interested in the course of philosophy in the Islamic world, both past and present, with a particular focus on the Persianate world. For some time, he has been committed to an approach to philosophy that focuses on spiritual exercises, following the work of the late Pierre Hadot. Increasingly, he is interested in how this study and category of philosophy coincides with the emergent category of global philosophy. In terms of method, his research is informed by the need for a decolonial and reparative study of Islam.

He supervises graduate students broadly in Islamic intellectual history, especially in philosophy, theology, and Qurʾanic exegesis.

He is currently interested in three projects: a monograph on Plato and Platonisms in Islam, a theological analysis of Imamology in Shiʿi thought, and the reception of some European philosophies in the postcolonial Muslim context.

With former student and colleague Ahab Bdaiwi, he is editing the Oxford Handbook of Shiʿi Islam.

He has advised various government departments and private-sector concerns on Iraq, Iran, Shiʿi Islam in the Gulf, and Islam in Britain and Europe.

He also runs a blog featuring his various reflections on philosophy, both Islamic and otherwise, as well as notes on manuscript research and related critical editions. The blog, entitled Hikmat, is available here.

Sheikh Mohammed Al-Hilli is a well-known Muslim Shia scholar and an international public speaker. He is the founder and Executive Director of Noor Islamic Education, one of the leading Islamic organisations based in United Kingdom, whose courses, videos and publications have reached millions across the world.

For over 20 years, Sheikh Al-Hilli has delivered lectures across the world, including North America, Africa, Europe, Australia as well as parts of Asia. He is the author of four books: Arbaeen the walk, Baqi: past present and future, Muharrams sermons as well as Secrets to Happiness.

Sheikh Al-Hilli is passionate in organising and running marriage and parenting courses as well as workshops for the youth. For example ‘The Successful Marriage Course’ has been running for 10 years both in person and online, with hundreds of participants across the world, and is the longest running course for marriage across the Western world. Sheikh is also the religious guide for several annual Ziyarah, Hajj and Umrah programmes.

is a scholar of the Middle East and South Asia. She specializes in the history of gender, sectarianism, and Shi’a Islam in national and transnational spaces.

Her current book manuscript analyzes how the seventh-century figure, Zaynab bint Ali, granddaughter of the Prophet Muhammed, has been used in 20th-century contexts, tracing the development and evolution of pilgrimage to two female shrines in Syria (the Sayeda Zaynab shrine) and Pakistan (Bibi Pak Daman) and prisons in Iraq as sites of memory and identity construction. Based on oral interviews, fieldwork and archival research in Syria, Pakistan, and Iraq, Prof. Zaidi’s work explores the physical and imaginative spaces in which identity is made and contested and shows how transnational narratives become embedded in local contexts.

Prof. Zaidi’s research has been supported by fellowships and grants from the Gerda Henkel Foundation, the SSRC, the Middle East Center at the University of Pennsylvania, as well as from the Dresher Center for the Humanities and UMBC’s Office of Research and Creative Achievement. Most recently, she has been awarded a National Endowment of the Humanities (NEH) yearlong fellowship to complete her book project.

At UMBC, Prof. Zaidi teaches a wide range of classes, from Hist 312 (The Modern Middle East) to Hist 386 (Hindus, Muslims, and their Others) and Hist 379 (Women, Gender, and Islam). She also teaches courses on Islamic empires and Islamic movements.

Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Miami. His research broadly considers the development of Islamic theology, historiography and debates on the caliphate. Husayn obtained his Ph.D. in Near Eastern Studies from Princeton University and an M.A. in Arabic and Islamic Studies from Harvard University. Husayn is the recipient of a Fulbright award and the University of Miami Fellowship in the Arts and Humanities. He is the author of Opposing the Imam (published in 2021) and Caliphate and Imamate (published in 2023). N.A. Husayn, Ph.D.,

Shaykh Azhar Nasser was born and raised in Michigan and has a degree in cultural anthropology from the University of Michigan. After completing his academic studies, he pursued his religious studies at the Hawza of Najaf under the offices of Grand Ayatollah Sistani and Grand Ayatollah Hakim.

In addition to his extensive study of classical religious texts, he has also taught introductory courses to western students at the seminary. Shaykh Azhar has a deep passion for the study of the Holy Quran which is evident from his lectures and discussions. Shaykh Azhar is the author of two books, “The Grand Tour: Quranic Descriptions of Paradise”, published in 2018 and “Spiritual Prescriptions”, published in 2019.

Sheikh Azhar is the Religious Director of Curriculum Planning. He is also a Co-Founder of Tasneem Institute.

Marzia Hassan (LLB, MSW, RSW) is a psychotherapist, marriage and family therapist, relationship consultant, parent coach, author, and public speaker based in Toronto, Canada. She has over two decades of experience supporting individuals, couples, parents, and families in building healthier and more meaningful relationships.

With a background in law and a Master of Social Work from the University of Toronto, Marzia combines evidence-based therapeutic approaches with spiritual wisdom to help people navigate relationship challenges, strengthen communication, and cultivate greater emotional well-being. Her work incorporates approaches including Emotionally Focused Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, mindfulness, and the Gottman Method.

She is also the author of Parenting in the Age of Facebook and is known for her work in parenting, marriage, family relationships, spirituality, and personal development. Through therapy, workshops, speaking engagements, and educational platforms, Marzia continues to empower individuals and families to move from conflict and disconnection toward greater understanding, connection, and cooperation.

Born in Karachi, Pakistan, Syed Jarry Haider Zaidi earned his Bachelor’s degree in 2012 from the Institute of Business Administration (IBA), Karachi—a premier institution originally established in academic partnership with the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. Following his graduation, he immigrated to Toronto, Canada, where he completed all three levels of the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation in 2017. For over twelve years, he has served as a Senior Operations Coordinator in the transport equipment industry.

Syed Jarry began his formal Islamic studies at age 13 at Zaynabia Madressah in Karachi, mastering foundational disciplines including Sarf, Nahw, Mantiq, and Fiqh. He continues his advanced Islamic education through an online Hawza curriculum, currently in his fourth year, alongside private study under various prominent scholars.

Over the past five years, Syed Jarry has delivered over 1,200 lectures at Islamic centers across Canada and the United States. He is also the author of numerous published books and articles in both Urdu and English defending and articulating Shia theology. Looking ahead, he plans to further his academic career by pursuing a doctorate in Islamic Studies.

Nouri Sardar is a poet and filmmaker born and raised in London, now residing in Dearborn, Michigan. His poetry focuses on the Ahlulbayt the Prophet Muhammad and his family), on divine love, spirituality and on issues of social justice. He has published seven books of poetry and produced multiple albums commemorating the epic of Ashura. Through books, albums and videos, his poetry is read and heard avidly by readers and listeners worldwide. As a filmmaker, Nouri has produced and directed dozens of documentaries and short films tackling various issues that affect the Muslim community.

Mayor Abdullah H. Hammoud has been an unwavering advocate for his hometown of Dearborn for over a decade. As the proud son of working class, immigrant parents, Mayor Hammoud was born and raised in Dearborn. As the city’s seventh mayor, Hammoud is deeply committed to building a city where residents in every corner have the opportunity to thrive and contribute to its success.

A product of Dearborn Public Schools and three-time graduate of the University of Michigan, Mayor Hammoud has master’s degrees in business administration and public health, and a bachelor’s degree in science.

Prior to his role as mayor, Abdullah Hammoud served as Dearborn’s State Representative in the Michigan House of Representatives, representing the 15th District. During his time in the state legislature, he championed various initiatives aimed at safeguarding air quality and public health, improving education, healthcare access, and economic development for the people of Michigan.

In November 2021, Abdullah Hammoud was elected as the Mayor of Dearborn, and has since been delivering on his shared vision of a more inclusive, vibrant, and prosperous community. As Mayor, Abdullah Hammoud has made historic investments in public parks; instituted public health in all policies; prioritized economic development and public safety; and innovated the way the government delivers services to its over 100 thousand Dearborn residents. Hammoud has fostered collaboration between the city government, local businesses, educational institutions, and community organizations.

In addition to his mayoral duties, Mayor Hammoud is a dedicated husband and father. He and his wife, Dr. Fatima Beydoun, are excited to raise their growing family in Dearborn.

Syed Mesum Abbas is a renowned international noha reciter and artist known for his powerful voice and lifelong dedication to the service of the Ahlulbayt (AS). Born and raised in New Jersey, USA, Mesum Abbas began his professional journey at a young age and has since become a respected voice within the global Shia community.

With a career spanning decades, he has released numerous albums and recitations that have reached audiences around the world. His work is deeply rooted in the remembrance of the Ahlulbayt (AS), with his recitations capturing the grief, devotion, and spirit of Karbala.

Mesum Abbas is also widely recognized for his role as a judge on The Shia Voice, the international talent program produced by Imam Hussein Media Group that showcases Quran recitation, poetry, nohas, and religious lectures. He has served as a judge since the show's inception, alongside prominent figures including Sayed Ammar Nakshawani and Mulla Nazar Qatari.

Through his recitations and continued involvement in The Shia Voice, Mesum Abbas has contributed to nurturing and encouraging a new generation of Shia artists and reciters, while continuing his own service to the Ahlulbayt (AS) through the timeless tradition of noha.

Resident Imam, Al-Abbas Islamic Centre, Birmingham, UK • Former Resident Imam in South Africa and Kenya

Education • BA in Islamic Philosophy and Mysticism • MA in Islamic Studies • Advanced Diploma in Counselling and Psychology • Qualified Civil and Commercial Mediator

Recognition & Awards • Voted UK’s Most Impactful Imam (2021) • Voted UK Religious Advocate of the Year (2024) • Voted Runner-up, UK Religious Advocate of the Year (2025)

Leadership & Civic Engagement • Member, Birmingham City Council Standing Advisory Council on Religious Education (2018 – Present) • Former Co-Chair, Citizens UK West Midlands County (2019 – 2023) • Elected National Trustee, Citizens UK (2020 – Present) • School Governor, Moseley School and Sixth Form (2019 – Present) • Member, West Midlands High Sheriff Nominations Committee ( from 2024 - Present) • Former Member, West Midlands Combined Authority Faith Strategic Partnership Group.

Co-Founder: Imamia Institute, Johanesburg , South Africa

Founder: Ummu Abeeha Centre, Kumasi, Ghana. Note: West Midlands is a county in the UK.

State Rep. Alabas Farhat proudly serves the 3rd House District, which comprises most of Dearborn and parts of Detroit. Farhat has a strong passion for public service, and he carries that dedication with him to Lansing as he advocates for both the residents in his district and for the wellbeing of all Michiganders across the state. Through his experience serving at all levels of government, Farhat has learned that real change starts with the people.

That’s why he immensely values listening to and working closely with residents — he believes this direct communication and close connection with constituents is the key to revitalizing the community, improving the standard of living for all and creating positive change for generations to come. In order to manifest these changes, Farhat knows public health, public safety, economic development and strong infrastructure must be central legislative priorities.

Mulla Ali Fadhil is a Islamic reciter and artist, known for popularizing English-language recitations and leading the development of English-language majalis. He grew up in Iraq, surviving wars by age twelve, and later worked as an interpreter for the U.S. Army and at Saddam Hussein's trial. Fadhil has gained a global following through his unique approach of incorporating English translations into his recitations, fostering deeper connections with diverse audiences worldwide

Qari Sayid Saif Al-Hussaini is a Toronto-based Qur’an reciter, voice educator, and founder of SV Academy, where he helps people develop their voices for Qur’an recitation, adhan, and nasheed. Through his recitations and educational content, he has built an international audience, sharing his passion for the beauty of the Qur’an and poetry, and making vocal training accessible to learners of all levels. His teaching combines practical vocal techniques with an emphasis on confidence, expression, and meaningful connection to the words being recited. Qari Saif’s work is guided by a simple belief: anyone can learn to recite beautifully.

Adam Fahs, MD, is a board-certified orthopedic surgeon specializing in orthopedic trauma and serving patients throughout the greater Detroit area. Born and raised in southeast Michigan, he is the son of immigrants from South Lebanon. Dr. Fahs is passionate about caring for patients with complex and life-altering injuries and helping them regain function and return to their lives.

Beyond his clinical practice and raising his three beautiful kids, Dr. Fahs has a strong interest in global and humanitarian medicine. In December 2023, he traveled to Gaza with one of the first international medical NGOs to enter the region following the October 7 escalation in the genocide, providing surgical care amid an unprecedented humanitarian crisis. He has also participated in two surgical missions to Lebanon, in 2025 and 2026.

He loves operating, he hates golf, and his ultimate goal is make his kids proud of daddy.

Abraham “Abe” Obeid is a Lebanese-American entrepreneur, content creator, and the founder of Halal Food Junkie, a food-media platform based in the Dearborn and Metro Detroit community. Obeid graduated from Central Michigan University in 2018 with a degree in Business Administration. He launched Halal Food Junkie in 2017, initially sharing his passion for food and highlighting halal restaurants, and eventually grew the platform into a recognizable brand focused on food, local businesses, culture, and community. His background in business has also carried into entrepreneurship, restaurant partnerships, marketing, and collaborations with local brands, helping Halal Food Junkie evolve beyond a traditional food-review page into a broader media and business platform.

Dr. Saleh Al-Ameen is a board-certified family physician, medical educator, and humanitarian who has devoted his career to the intersection of medicine, faith, and cultural heritage. He serves as Clinical Assistant Professor at Wayne State University School of Medicine and is the Founder and Director of the International Medical League, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit expanding healthcare access to underserved communities in the U.S. and abroad.

Dr. Al-Ameen traces his roots to Jabal Aamel in south Lebanon, a region deeply tied to Islamic scholarship, and descends from a lineage of respected religious scholars, including his great-grandfathers Ayatollah Sayed Mohsen Al-Ameen and Ayatollah Sayed Mohammad Ali Al-Ameen.

Keeping true to that lineage and its sense of obligation toward the oppressed, Dr. Al-Ameen has built a career at the intersection of faith and service. His medical mission work includes providing care to Arbaeen pilgrims at the shrine of Imam Hussein (AS) in Iraq. Since 2022, he has also led medical missions to Lebanon, continuing throughout the recent war in Lebanon and its aftermath at a pace of three missions per year. These efforts — bringing physicians, nurses, and mental health professionals to rural and displaced communities — have served more than 5,000 patients to date. His work carries forward a family tradition of scholarship and service as medicine in action for communities in crisis.

Dr. Al-Ameen will speak to conditions on the ground, the challenges facing communities in conflict, and how the global Shia community can support relief efforts and chart a path forward.

Dr. Sayeda Elhaam Jawadi is a family medicine resident, community organizer, activist, and health educator. She earned her medical degree from The Pennsylvania State University College of Medicine and is completing her residency at Temple University. She has dedicated her career to serving Imam al-Mahdi (atfs), with the goal of establishing a clinic in his name to provide accessible medical care to underserved patients.

She is also committed to addressing barriers to healthcare access through policy and advocacy. Throughout her education and medical training, she has worked in free clinics serving marginalized and immigrant communities. She recently authored and successfully passed a policy through the Pennsylvania Medical Society to reduce barriers for healthcare professionals who wear the hijab in the operating room. She hopes to continue using health policy to expand access to medical care.

Ali Aljarrah is a civil rights leader and policy advocate for working-class New Jerseyans. As senior adviser at CAIR Action NJ, he has helped win some of the biggest policy fights in the state over the last few years, protecting First Amendment rights, enshrining immigrant protections into state law, and fighting for legislation to make polluters pay for damages from climate change.

Born and raised in Passaic County to Iraqi immigrant parents, Ali learned the importance of giving back at a young age, and he's dedicated his life to fighting for families like his. His work spans policy advocacy and sustainability, from securing climate resilience funding for communities across the country to helping families and small businesses lower their energy bills.

Now he's running for Passaic County Commissioner to build more affordable homes and protect renters, fix dangerous roads and connect our communities, expand food assistance and improve social services, and protect our rights and stand up to the Trump administration.

Dr. Syed Mehdi Husaini is a resident physician training in neurology currently based at the University of Massachusetts where he is part of the Global Health, Social Advocacy, and Justice Track in his training program. He is involved in several academic, community health, and teaching projects as well as a site investigator for a major clinical trial.

Dr. Husaini has been giving lectures about Islam and the Ahlul Bayt at Islamic and at interfaith gatherings for many years. He continues a program of study at Al Hujjah Islamic seminary to continue to advance his religious knowledge and most recently, he has begun a series of Islamic educational community workshops in conjunction with Muslims4Peace.

He earned a medical degree from Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School where he graduated in 2024 as a Dean’s Scholar with distinction as part of the Gold Humanism Honor Society for his excellence in patient care. In medical school he served in Student Government while also holding leadership positions in the student free clinic.

Within medicine, he has a passion for neurology and cerebrovascular disease, specifically seeking opportunities in community health and institutional leadership to improve patient care, while also exploring the intersection of faith and medicine.

Syed Muhammad Shabbar Zaidi is a distinguished Pakistani chartered accountant, economist, author, and former public servant. A graduate of Hailey College of Commerce, University of the Punjab, he is a Fellow Member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP), where he served as President from 2005–2006. He also served as President of the South Asian Federation of Accountants in 2008.

Throughout his career, Syed Shabbar Zaidi has held prominent positions in Pakistan's financial and public sectors. He served as caretaker Minister for Finance, Board of Revenue, and Excise & Taxation in the Government of Sindh in 2013 and later served as Chairman of the Federal Board of Revenue from 2019–2020. He also spent many years with A.F. Ferguson & Co., a member firm of PwC, including as Territory Senior Partner.

Beyond his professional career, Syed Shabbar Zaidi is an accomplished author whose works explore Pakistan's economy, taxation, governance, and broader social and intellectual issues. His books include A Journey for Clarity, Pakistan: Not a Failed State, Panama Leaks: A Blessing in Disguise, Rich People, Poor Country, Faith & Intellect and The Serene Self. He has recently also written his autobiography by the name of 32 Onkar Road. He has also contributed to nonprofit institutions, including the Sindh Institute of Urology & Transplantation and Liaquat National Hospital.

A son of Gwinnett County, proudly serving a proud product of its public schools, its communities, and its culture. Someone who believes that real progress gets made together.

From serving as Gwinnett County Democratic Party’s First Vice Chair, to organizing local campaigns as your neighbor, and now as your State Representative in the GA General Assembly, my work has always functioned on one core belief:

LEADERSHIP IS NOT ABOUT TITLES, IT’S ABOUT THOSE AROUND YOU I took this belief to the GA General Assembly, where I routinely champion our community through consistent outreach, down-to-earth policy proposals, and putting District 106’s needs first. Having worked to pass legislation such as gas tax suspensions, HOA reforms, and measures to support public education.

While holding a bachelor’s degree from Kennesaw State University in political science and public relations, I also am a young entrepreneur. Knowing the value of hard work, I was able to launch and run a successful business that I begun at age 20. I know what it means to build something from the ground up, and I take that principle everywhere I go.

That same principle is what has allowed me to proudly serve District 106, the cities of Lawrenceville and Snellville since 2025.

Nabaa Baher is currently completing her Bachelor’s degree at the University of Windsor. Alongside her academic pursuits, she has developed a deep passion for Islamic studies, studying under esteemed scholars such as Sayed Ammar Nakshawani, Sheikh Azhar Nasser, Sayed Mohammed Baqir Al-Qazwini, and Sheikh Mahdi Rastani. She continues to broaden her understanding through certified Islamic courses that explore subjects including the tafsir of supplications, the theology of human suffering, the history of the Infallibles (as), and contemporary issues in Islamic law. In recognition of her dedication to Islamic education and oratory, Nabaa was honoured to be a finalist in The Shia Voice competition of 2025. Public speaking has long been one of her greatest passions. Under the mentorship of Sayed Ammar Nakshawani, Sayed Mohammed Baqir Al-Qazwini, and Sayed Hassan Qazwini, she has received formal training to refine the depth, delivery, and emotional resonance of her lectures. Nabaa has had the privilege of addressing audiences across the United Kingdom, Canada, and the United States—delivering English majalis complemented by Arabic recitations and supplications.

As she continues her journey of faith and learning, Nabaa aspires to grow as both a student and a servant of the Ahlulbayt (as).

Dr. Hassan Abbas is the Distinguished Professor of International Relations at the Near East South Asia Strategic Studies Centre (NESA) at the National Defense University (NDU) in Washington DC. He serves as a senior advisor at Project on Shi’ism and Global Affairs at Harvard University’s Weatherhead Center for International Affairs, and his current research work focuses on building narratives for countering political and religious extremism as well as rule of law reforms in developing states. Previously, he served as professor and department chair at NDU’s College of International Security Affairs (2011-2019) and as the Distinguished Quaid-i-Azam Professor at Columbia University (2009-2011). He holds a PhD. from the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts University, an LLM in International Law from the Nottingham University, UK and a M.A. in Political Science from Punjab University, Pakistan.

Sayyid Mehboob Mehdi Abidi al-Najafi, son of Hujjatul Islam Sayyid Abul Hashim Abidi, was born in India and raised in Najaf, Iraq, where he studied under prominent scholars. After migrating to India due to political unrest, he continued his Islamic education at Jamia Nazimia, earning a master’s degree and later pursuing advanced studies in Qom and Najaf.

A respected scholar, and author fluent in Urdu, Arabic, Farsi, and English, Sayyid Abidi has served as editor-in-chief of Al-Ghadir magazine and led a popular Quran Commentary Class for over seventeen years. He is the founder of Hadi School of Excellence and the International Baqee Organization and oversees several community projects.

Currently, he serves as the Resident Scholar of the Islamic Education Center (Husaini) in Chicago, under the guidance of Ayatullah al-Sayyid Ali al-Husseini al-Sistani, and is an active member of national Shia scholarly organizations in North America.

Faraz Hasan Zaidi was born and raised in Queens, New York, and is currently a medical student at Rutgers New Jersey Medical School. He holds a Master of Science in Biomedical Sciences with a distinction in pharmacology, and is pursuing Islamic studies at Mufid Seminary. Faraz is the founder and president of the Advanced Learning Institute of New Jersey, a non-profit charity organization dedicated to education and development within the Shia Muslim community. Alongside his research in global surgery, he leads the Student Family Health Care Center at University Hospital, where he helps provide accessible healthcare to underserved communities.

Mr Wasif Rizvi is the founding president of Habib University. Mr. Rizvi has led the vision of the first liberal arts institution of higher learning in Pakistan. Habib University, under his leadership, has become a globally recognized and appreciated university with established collaborations with leading institutions – including Carnegie Mellon University and Texas A&M University at Qatar, Stanford University, University of Michigan, and the Claremont Consortium of Liberal Arts Colleges. His achievements are visible by Habib University’s unmatched global partnerships, distinguished faculty, well recognized curriculum, exponentially growing number of student applications and an innovative campus design that received accolade and international awards of excellence in Planning for New Campus. Mr Rizvi has been involved in various areas of education development in the developing world for the last two decades. Prior to initiating the Habib University project, he had led Aga Khan Education Service in Pakistan and many other development projects in Asia and Africa. Mr Rizvi holds twin graduate degrees from Harvard Kennedy School and Harvard School of Education.

Mustafa Alsultany is an Iraqi-American videographer, editor, content creator, and the founder of The Babylon Collection. Deeply rooted in cultural preservation and narrative storytelling, Mustafa collaborates with Stand With Dignity to produce impactful Shia media—documenting key events, perspectives, and community moments across Metro Detroit, New York, New Jersey, and Washington, D.C.

Beyond his community documentary work, Mustafa creates engaging digital media alongside Abe Obeid for Halal Food Junkie, highlighting local cuisine, small businesses, and community culture, while also producing commercial media for Own It Realty and Hassan Scheib. As the creative mind behind The Babylon Collection, he bridges media production with heritage fashion, designing apparel—such as the iconic Babylon Iraq Jersey—that honors Iraqi history and allows individuals to wear their pride.

Dr. Hyder Ihsan Mirza earned his Bachelor of Science in Nursing from the University of Detroit Mercy in 2020. During his undergraduate studies, he founded and served as president of the university's MEDLIFE chapter, directing medical and developmental initiatives in South America. He then spent two years as a critical care and trauma nurse at Henry Ford Hospital in Detroit before completing his Doctor of Nursing Practice in Nurse Anesthesia at Rosalind Franklin University in 2025.

Dr. Mirza remains deeply committed to international humanitarian medical care, having served on surgical missions to the West Bank, Palestine (November 2025) and South Lebanon (June 2026). He aims to integrate regular global humanitarian service as a cornerstone of his professional career.

Dr. Vinay Khetia is an accomplished academic who has taken great strides in the field of religious studies. With his exceptional qualifications, including a PhD in Religious Studies from McMaster University and an MA in History and Philosophy of Religion from Concordia University. Dr. Khetia has had his published works on Islamic law and exegesis. In particular, his areas of interest include Twelver Shi’ism, which has become a focal point for his studies. What sets Dr. Khetia apart is his dedication and perseverance in pursuing his studies in various universities and Islamic seminaries over 20 years. This dedication and passion are evident in his guest lecture at Harvard University and as a lecturer at both McMaster University and the University of Toronto. Dr. Khetia is currently the academic director at the Shia Research Institute in Toronto.

After Maghrib Media Group is a creative Islamic media team focused on bringing fresh, meaningful, and engaging content to a new generation. Founded by Ahmed Gokal, Sayed Ali Radhawi, and Mojtaba, the team brings together years of experience in media and creative production.

With a vision to move beyond traditional approaches to Islamic media, After Maghrib creates content designed to connect with Gen Z and beyond—making Islamic storytelling something audiences can learn from, relate to, and genuinely look forward to.

Dr. Ali Nasrallah, MD, is a board-certified Family Medicine physician, educator, and community advocate dedicated to making high-quality healthcare accessible and personal. He is the founder and Medical Director of The Family Doc Clinic & Urgent Care, where he leads a growing team of healthcare professionals providing comprehensive primary care, urgent care, preventive services, and community-based healthcare.

A Dearborn native and graduate of Fordson High School, Dr. Nasrallah attended the University of Michigan–Ann Arbor, where he studied Biopsychology, Cognition, and Neuroscience with a minor in Community Action and Social Change. He went on to attend the University of Michigan Medical School as a Brehm Scholar before completing his Family Medicine residency at Beaumont Wayne, where he served as Chief Resident.

In addition to his clinical work, Dr. Nasrallah is actively involved in medical education, teaching and mentoring future physicians through Wayne State University and Authority Health. His work has been recognized through numerous honors, including the American Academy of Family Physicians Award for Excellence, the President’s Volunteer Service Award, the Zaman International Spirit of Hope Award, the University of Michigan Medical School Research Excellence Award, and recognition as an Hour Detroit Top Doc.

Beyond the clinic, Dr. Nasrallah is deeply committed to community service and health education. Through The Family Doc, he works to make healthcare information understandable and accessible to the public while organizing and participating in initiatives such as free sports physicals, health screenings, and services for underserved and uninsured communities.

At the center of his work is a simple philosophy: family medicine is about more than treating illness—it is about building relationships, preventing disease, educating patients, and being a trusted advocate for individuals and families throughout every stage of life.

Zakira Shyrose Jaffer Dhalla, B.A (hons), M.Ed., is a graduate of York University (Toronto, Canada) and holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Psychology and Sociology and a Master’s Degree in the field of Education.

She lectures on Islam at mosques, universities, churches and interfaith gatherings and also recites majalises in Urdu, English and Gujarati.

Shyrose Jaffer Dhalla is an internationally well-known “Zakira” or Islamic lecturer and is the recipient of Ahlulbayt TV’s “2012 Award of Excellence” for her outstanding contribution to female public speaking. The award was presented to her at a prestigious event in London, England and was broadcast on LIVE TV around the world.

She is also recipient of the Islamic Centre of North America (ICNA) “Woman of Wonder” award (2017) as well as the “Woman of Inspiration” Award (2014) by Toronto’s Radio Pro-Learning program.

Maulana Syed Muhammad Ali Najafi is a respected Shia Islamic scholar and speaker known for his engaging lectures on the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (AS), Islamic faith, spirituality, and contemporary issues facing the Muslim community. Based between Denmark and Canada, he has been invited to deliver Muharram and religious programs at various Shia Islamic centers and communities.

Through his lectures, Maulana Syed Muhammad Ali Najafi seeks to connect the teachings and legacy of the Ahlulbayt (AS) with the lives and experiences of Muslims today, encouraging audiences toward greater faith, reflection, and spiritual growth.

As Executive Vice President, Canadian Personal Banking Digital Transformation and Strategy, Rizwan brings a wealth of experience, fostering a culture of technological advancement and customer-centric solutions. His current role focuses on overseeing the bank's digital transformation, leveraging technology and business innovations to drive customer and colleague engagement. His leadership is key in developing robust innovation ecosystems that include colleague ideation, incubation, acceleration, partnerships with fintechs and big techs, and a focus on enhancing TD's patent portfolio. Beyond his role in digital transformation, Rizwan is passionate about empowering all segments of society to maximize their potential through inclusion, education, and mentorship, thereby strengthening community bonds.

Khanum Syeda Asma ‘Abidi is a religious scholar (ʿĀlima), educator, and counselor affiliated with the Islamic Education Center (IEC) of the Husaini Association of Greater Chicago. She provides faith-based guidance and counseling to women on religious, ethical, family, and personal matters in both individual and group settings.

She holds a Master’s degree in Islamic Studies and a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, as well as a Diploma in Early Childhood Education.

Her formal Islamic education includes studies at Madrassa-tul Qaim and Jamia-tuz Zahra Islamic Seminary. She continues her advanced Hawza studies under distinguished scholars from Qom and Najaf.

Khanum Asma regularly conducts Dars sessions, Qur’an study circles, lectures, and educational workshops on a wide range of Islamic, spiritual, and contemporary topics for women and youth, both in person and online. She has been invited to lecture and recite Majālis at Islamic centers in various cities across the United States, Canada, and Australia.

She is the Co-Founder of Al-Kauthar Institute, an educational initiative dedicated to promoting Islamic learning and fostering the intellectual and spiritual development of women and youth in the light of the Qur’an and the teachings of the Ahlul Bayt (عليهم السلام). Her work places particular emphasis on religious literacy, women’s education and empowerment, ethical development, strong family values, and the practical application of Islamic teachings in contemporary life.

Dr. Sheikh Faiyaz Jaffer is the Executive Director for the Islamic Center and University Chaplain at New York University. He holds a doctorate in education from NYU, with a focus on the identity development of Muslim Minorities demographics in the United States. Pursuing the classical course of Islamic education, he studied in the Seminary of Karbala, Iraq, one of the most prominent centers for Islamic learning.

As a faith leader and social activist, Dr. Sheikh Jaffer has lectured at various universities, seminars, and workshops across the United States, Canada, Europe, East Africa, and the Middle East. As a highly sought-after lecturer and religious leader, he regularly leads prayer services and delivers sermons across North America. Due to the political and social climate, he has been making strides in the greater New York area by taking part in several interfaith seminars and discussions with the goal of increasing dialogue with faith leaders. In 2019, Dr. Sheikh Jaffer co-founded Pillars of Peace, a non-profit established in order to address a gap in appropriate services for survivors of domestic and gender-based violence from all backgrounds and in particular within the Muslim community. In addition to his roles at NYU’s Islamic Center, Dr. Shaykh Jaffer serves as a Professor of Public Service of NYU’s Robert F. Wagner Graduate School of Public Service, where he teaches courses on Islamic Law and Islamic Spirituality and a Visiting Professor at the Bayan Graduate School.

Sayed Ali Khalkhali, born in London, studied both his primary and secondary education at Al-Sadiq and Al-Zahra School. After successfully completing his A-Levels at Woodhouse college, he studied Pharmacy at University of London, School of Pharmacy.

In addition, Sayed Ali has taught for more than 15 years at Alulbayt Islamic School, in addition to Islamic sessions & study circles with regular members of the local community. Sayed Ali has also been a youth mentor in local youth clubs, supporting young and vulnerable children.

Sayed Ali successfully completed his Masters degree in Islamic studies in Middlesex University, London. With his final paper on alcohol in cough medicine, under the supervision of Ayatollah Sayed Fadhil Milani, and studied in the Islamic Seminary (Hawza). Sayed Ali is pursuing his Islamic education further, and wishes to continue at every stage, and level granted, Inshallah.

A servant of the Ahlulbayt is what he wishes to remain as, and to serve at every level for the Ahlulbayt is an honour that we can never measure.

Sarah Kermalli graduated from UofT with an honours in bio and psych. What she gained from her experience as a student was how stress can have a dramatic impact on the body. She has completed comprehensive training in both Mat and Reformer Pilates and continues educating herself on Post and Pre Rehab protocols for the knee and back as well as Postural Analysis.

Wellness by Saarah is a wellness-focused platform dedicated to helping individuals build healthier, more balanced, and intentional lifestyles. Through an approachable and holistic perspective on wellness, Saarah creates content that encourages her community to prioritize their physical, mental, and overall well-being.

With a focus on making wellness accessible and practical, Wellness by Saarah aims to inspire meaningful lifestyle changes while empowering individuals to feel their best from the inside out.

Shabir Mukhtar is a dedicated community leader, entrepreneur, and philanthropist with a proven record of service and impact. He has spearheaded numerous charitable initiatives that provide both immediate relief and long-term support to families affected by poverty, displacement, and natural disasters. His efforts emphasize sustainable solutions such as housing, education, and empowerment programs that uplift and strengthen communities locally and internationally.

In addition to his charitable work, Shabir is a successful entrepreneur with diverse ventures. He is the owner of a men’s fashion store specializing,fine menswear, has owned and managed multiple auto repair shops, and is actively engaged in real estate development and investment. Across each of these fields, he has built a reputation for quality, innovation, and commitment to serving others.

Beyond business, Shabir is deeply committed to his community. He regularly helps and empowers local members by providing mentorship, resources, and opportunities for advancement. Through his leadership in philanthropy, business, and real estate, Shabir continues to create lasting value, inspire others, and build pathways of hope and success.

Fatima Abdi, MPH is a trained Infectious Disease Epidemiologist, with an MPH in Epidemiology and certificate in Maternal / Child Health. Her work experience is at the CDC Foundation and California Department of Public Health. She is a co-founder of Wonder and Wilayah, a faith-rooted community initiative that nurtures sacred connection, learning, and service through the lens of the Ahl al-Bayt (a). Additionally, Fatima also runs Yaqeen Book Club, a Shi’a ladies book club based in New Jersey.

Rida Fatima currently serves as the Fundraising and Outreach Coordinator at Al-Kisa Foundation, where she leads initiatives to strengthen donor relations, expand community engagement, and promote sustainable impact. Over the past five years with Al-Kisa, she has contributed in multiple capacities, including serving as Operations Director of Rise Institute. With more than twelve years of experience in the nonprofit sector, Rida has dedicated her career to advancing faith-based and community initiatives. Her work focuses on connecting people and purpose—creating opportunities for individuals and organizations to make a lasting social impact.

Qunoot Almecci is an education strategist who brings a systems-level perspective to educational innovation and institutional effectiveness. She serves as Educational Advisor at RISE Institute, Associate Professor of Medical Education, and Principal Consultant at Down For Learning. She holds a Doctor of Education and a Master of Science, with professional certifications in Medical Education and Appreciative Advising. Her scholarship and professional contributions reflect a sustained commitment to educational excellence.

Faraz Zaidi is the Founder and Creative Director of FOUND, a globally recognized American luxury fashion house shaped by his Pakistani-American and Muslim identity.

Over the past decade, Faraz has built FOUND from an independent creative vision into a global fashion brand, carried by iconic institutions such as Harrods and leading luxury retailers around the world. His work has been embraced by some of the most influential figures across every medium of culture, while FOUND has collaborated on globally recognized collections with some of the world’s largest and most prominent brands.

Drawing from South Asian heritage, personal memory, and the experience of growing up between cultures, Faraz has developed a distinct visual language that challenges conventional ideas of what American luxury can look like. Through FOUND, he is expanding the space for Muslim and South Asian stories within global culture and demonstrating the power of identity as a source of creativity, ambition, and cultural influence.

PRESIDENT Dr. Azmat Husain is an experienced physician executive having served in leadership roles in both hospital and physician practice management. He has served as Chairman of Emergency, Regional Medical Director, Senior Vice President of a health system as well as most recently Chief Executive Officer of a 2-hospital health system physician practice. He also served on Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro’s transition team on healthcare. His accomplishments in the field of healthcare have been covered by numerous media outlets such as the Philadelphia Business Journal, MDLive, Bloomberg News, NPR and NBC. He currently is serving as Chief Medical Officer of his own healthcare company, Personic Health, that operates multispecialty physician practices in 10 states.

He has been active with several Shia Muslim organizations for the past 20 years serving on the board of directors of UMAA, Idara-e-Jaferia, Islamic Information Center and Global Caregivers. He has also been involved in significant philanthropic projects operating an elementary school for over 200 children in Najaf, Iraq as well as helping to establish the first Emergency Medicine physician training program for the country of Iraq.

Vice President, UMAA

Mustafa Abdi serves as Vice President of the Universal Muslim Association of America (UMAA) and is an active leader within the organization’s Board of Directors. Professionally, he works in Fiscal Management and Planning for the Department of Human Services, bringing over 20 years of executive experience across government, healthcare, telecommunications, and finance.

A dedicated civic advocate, Mustafa is deeply active in political organizing, interfaith coalition building, and social justice initiatives across North America. He is the co-founder of Muslims for Peace and Stand With Dignity—grassroots organizations dedicated to interfaith dialogue, civic engagement, and human rights advocacy—and serves on the Board of Trustees for The Children’s Home Society of New Jersey.

Recognized for his civil service and philanthropic leadership, Mustafa was awarded the prestigious Jefferson Award for Public Service. He holds both a Master of Science in Management Technology and a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Finance from the New Jersey Institute of Technology (NJIT). Through his work with UMAA and broader civic institutions, he remains steadfastly committed to empowering Muslim communities, advancing policy dialogue, and advocating for social justice.

Vice President, UMAA Syed Rizvi is a visionary CEO and transformational business leader with over 15 years of international experience driving multi-million-dollar growth, retail expansion, and enterprise transformation across health, consumer goods, and technology sectors. Known for turning strategy into measurable execution, he has led global initiatives for brands such as Samsung, Philips, Motorola, Walmart, and ASDA across North America, the Middle East, and South Asia.

Beyond his corporate achievements, Syed remains deeply rooted in community service. Each year, he opens his home for the remembrance of Imam Hussain, providing a space of unity and dignity for all. His quiet philanthropy and sustained commitment to community initiatives continue to benefit countless people

Rida Rizvi is an Operational Consultant in the Education sphere that focuses on building bridges amongst communities. Her current projects are supporting a Christian church-based preschool in improving leadership operations and managing all Operations for the Resistance Studies Series which was founded in 2025 by Karen Attiah, the former Editor of the World Opinions column at The Washington Post. She began her career in public policy working in the renewable energy sector with a special focus on solar energy. She worked on legislation or regulation in every deregulated state in the country. After the birth of her first child in 2013, she shifted gears to community organizing by co-founding a holistic, Islamic preschool and completing a year long interfaith fellowship at the Institute of Islamic, Christian, and Jewish Studies. Rida enjoys travel with her family which consists of her husband and 3 daughters.

Khurshaid Kazmi is an experienced leader with nearly 30 years of leadership experience overseeing operations in the pharmaceutical industry and facility management. He was the Vice President of Operations for nearly 20 years at Pharmaceutics International Incorporated prior to continuing on as Head of Operations for Modavar Pharmaceuticals.

He has also been serving an integral role in the UMAA convention for the past 20 years leading convention logistics and operations.

For nearly two decades, Rahat Husain has advocated on behalf of Shia Muslim communities before the White House, members of Congress, federal agencies, think tanks, NGOs, policy institutes, and academic experts. In 2015, during a private White House meeting with President Barack Obama, he raised the persecution and killing of Shia Muslims around the globe. His advocacy has also included engagement with the Trump and Biden administrations and interfaith work involving His Holiness the Dalai Lama. Rahat currently serves as Executive Director of the Shia Muslim Foundation and has held leadership roles with the Universal Muslim Association of America and the Islamic Information Center, including serving as Director of Legal and Policy Affairs at UMAA Advocacy and Executive Director of the Islamic Information Center, where he managed its American Leadership Initiative for Muslims.

Rahat is an attorney and longtime writer on Islam, American Muslim civic engagement, public policy, and international affairs. He has written as a columnist for The Washington Times and CDN News and has spent much of his career bringing Shia Muslim perspectives into American policy and civic discussions. His work through SMF, UMAA, IIC, and other community efforts has addressed religious freedom, anti Shia persecution, civil rights, immigration, mosque security, humanitarian issues, and stronger engagement between Muslim communities and American institutions.

Alvena Jeffery has a background in psychology and began her professional journey working in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), supporting children with autism. She later transitioned into the nonprofit sector, where she developed a strong passion for community service. She currently serves as a Logistics Coordinator and works with Muslim nonprofit organizations to support programs and initiatives that strengthen and serve the community.

Outside of her professional work, Alvena is a wife and mother of three boys who enjoys staying active, baking, and spending time with her family. Her commitment to service and community continues to be an important part of who she is.

Dr. Rumla Rizvi is a Specialty Clinical Pharmacist at Yale New Haven Health, where she works as part of a multidisciplinary team to provide patient-centered care, optimize medication therapy, and improve health outcomes.

Beyond her professional work, Rumla is deeply committed to community service and leadership. She joined UMAA in 2023 as a volunteer lead and currently serves on the UMAA Board, contributing to the organization’s programming and community initiatives. She has also led the Jafaria Youth Group in Connecticut and served as the Connecticut lead for the “Who Is Hussain?” campaign. In addition, Rumla is actively involved in organizing and facilitating ziyaraat trips for community members.

Outside of her professional and community commitments, Rumla enjoys traveling, baking and experimenting with desserts, exploring new places and cuisines, and spending time with family and friends. She especially enjoys combining her love for travel, community, and faith through meaningful experiences and gatherings.
